criteria.text: Can the selected AI workflow identify the correct configuration item without confusing duplicate, obsolete or incorrectly classified records?
criteria.why: Incorrect configuration identity can lead to an unsuitable service classification or impact result.
criteria.evidence: Sample configuration item matches, identification checks and duplicate review.
criteria.improve: Check identification rules and correct ambiguous or duplicated records.
criteria.learn: Whether the intended AI activity can reliably recognise the correct configuration item, rather than use a duplicate or outdated record as operational context.

criteria.text: Are the configuration items relevant to this workflow linked to the correct services and service offerings?
criteria.why: AI categorisation and service context depend on usable service associations.
criteria.evidence: Sample incident mappings and relevant CSDM relationships.
criteria.improve: Review and correct the mappings for the services in your pilot.
criteria.learn: Whether service and service offering context associated with the relevant configuration items can be trusted for routing, classification or investigation.

criteria.text: For AI impact analysis, do the relevant configuration items have valid and correctly directed dependency paths to impacted services?
criteria.why: Topology based impact analysis needs trustworthy dependency direction and coverage.
criteria.evidence: Dependency paths compared with known service impacts.
criteria.improve: Remediate the relationships used by your intended impact scenarios.
criteria.learn: Whether the dependency paths needed by AI assisted impact analysis are available and reflect known service effects.

criteria.text: Are the configuration attributes and relationships consumed by AI sufficiently accurate, current and traceable to maintained sources?
criteria.why: Stale or conflicting source data weakens AI context and conclusions.
criteria.evidence: Source timestamps, reconciliation review and selected record checks.
criteria.improve: Correct stale records and establish appropriate source refresh controls.
criteria.learn: Whether the configuration facts supplied to AI are current enough, accurate enough and traceable to maintained sources.

criteria.text: Is someone accountable for correcting configuration or service relationship defects discovered during AI evaluation?
criteria.why: The reliability of AI context depends on a repeatable way of fixing defects.
criteria.evidence: Named owner, improvement records and examples of resolved defects.
criteria.improve: Assign a data owner and introduce a tracked defect correction process.
criteria.learn: Whether discovered configuration defects can be corrected through accountable ownership before they recur in AI outputs.

criteria.text: Can the intended AI identity access the required configuration information while restricted records remain protected?
criteria.why: A workflow needs authorised access to relevant context without inappropriate disclosure.
criteria.evidence: Positive and negative access tests using the intended identities.
criteria.improve: Review role access and test permitted and denied retrieval paths.
criteria.learn: Whether AI can obtain the required configuration context while protected records remain unavailable to unauthorised identities.

criteria.text: Do approved articles cover the actual questions and incident categories selected for this AI capability?
criteria.why: Content outside the selected demand patterns does not support useful answers or resolutions.
criteria.evidence: Top incident categories and queries mapped to relevant published articles.
criteria.improve: Prioritise coverage of the common scoped incidents and questions.
criteria.learn: Whether approved knowledge covers the real questions and incident categories within the chosen AI scope. Missing coverage becomes a priority for knowledge preparation.

criteria.text: For selected incident types, are the instructions complete, ordered and usable by the intended audience?
criteria.why: Autonomous investigation requires repeatable procedures, not merely topic descriptions.
criteria.evidence: Subject matter review and walkthrough of sample diagnosis and resolution steps.
criteria.improve: Rewrite procedures with prerequisites, diagnostic steps and expected results.
criteria.learn: Whether the selected incident procedures contain enough ordered detail for an AI assistant or specialist to follow safely and consistently.

criteria.text: Are operational decisions, exceptions, unsafe conditions and escalation triggers documented rather than known only to experienced staff?
criteria.why: The tacit tax arises when the knowledge AI needs remains informal and inaccessible.
criteria.evidence: Analyst interviews, exception tables, policy conditions and escalation walkthroughs.
criteria.improve: Capture undocumented decision rules, exceptions and escalation boundaries.
criteria.learn: Whether undocumented analyst judgement, exceptions and escalation rules would create gaps when work is delegated to AI.

criteria.text: Have relevant articles been validated for accuracy and contradictions against current operational practice?
criteria.why: Conflicting or incorrect instructions can make grounded answers unreliable.
criteria.evidence: Article owner sign off and sampled comparison with real working practices.
criteria.improve: Resolve contradictory guidance and validate material instructions with service owners.
criteria.learn: Whether the knowledge used for generated answers and resolution steps is accurate and free from conflicting instructions.

criteria.text: Are the relevant articles clearly structured, described by metadata and maintained through a review process?
criteria.why: Well structured, current content improves retrievability and interpretation.
criteria.evidence: Article templates, metadata completeness, review dates and stale content reports.
criteria.improve: Apply consistent templates and establish scheduled maintenance.
criteria.learn: Whether relevant articles are organised and maintained so that the intended AI experience can interpret and retrieve them reliably.

criteria.text: Can the selected AI experience retrieve the relevant published articles through its configured search sources and profiles?
criteria.why: A correct article offers no value if the AI experience cannot find it.
criteria.evidence: Index status, source and search profile configuration, query test results.
criteria.improve: Correct indexing and search profile configuration, then test representative queries.
criteria.learn: Whether the AI Search configuration actually retrieves suitable published articles for representative questions.

criteria.text: Do knowledge retrieval and generated responses respect the intended user and agent access restrictions?
criteria.why: Restricted articles must not appear in responses to unauthorised users.
criteria.evidence: Positive and negative access tests with appropriate identities and content classes.
criteria.improve: Fix access controls and retest restricted retrieval before any pilot.
criteria.learn: Whether knowledge retrieval and generated responses protect restricted information for the relevant user and agent identities.

criteria.text: Are active catalogue items available for the request types the selected AI experience must recognise or fulfil?
criteria.why: AI needs a valid target for intended requests and redirection.
criteria.evidence: Request demand mapped to active items and allowed requester audiences.
criteria.improve: Prioritise missing items for common request intents.
criteria.learn: Whether valid catalogue destinations exist for the requests the AI experience is expected to recognise or fulfil.

criteria.text: Are catalogue item names, descriptions and guidance clear enough for AI to distinguish similar requests?
criteria.why: Ambiguous item descriptions increase incorrect request selection.
criteria.evidence: Item metadata review and sample utterance matching checks.
criteria.improve: Clarify labels, descriptions, eligibility and alternative request paths.
criteria.learn: Whether the intended AI experience can distinguish similar catalogue items using their descriptions and eligibility information.

criteria.text: Do the items selected for conversational ordering meet the requirements of the chosen Catalog Agent experience?
criteria.why: Unsupported item configurations fall back to a form or prevent a full conversation.
criteria.evidence: Conversational coverage report and checks for supported variables and scripting.
criteria.improve: Review item eligibility for the specific mechanism and keep safe form fallback.
criteria.learn: Whether selected items can be handled by the specific conversational catalogue capability, rather than unexpectedly falling back to forms.

criteria.text: Can the conversation collect and correctly validate the mandatory information needed to submit those requests?
criteria.why: Incomplete or incorrectly mapped variables produce failed or unsuitable requests.
criteria.evidence: Variable mapping tests, mandatory field scenarios and conditional input examples.
criteria.improve: Simplify variables or implement supported validation and dialogue flows.
criteria.learn: Whether the conversational flow can collect complete, valid request data before submission.

criteria.text: Are user eligibility, entitlements and approval rules enforced by the underlying ServiceNow workflow?
criteria.why: An AI recommendation must not bypass access and approval controls.
criteria.evidence: Request impersonation cases, positive and negative authorisation tests, approval history.
criteria.improve: Enforce user criteria and approvals at platform level, then retest.
criteria.learn: Whether the platform enforces requester eligibility and approval policies even when the request begins in an AI conversation.

criteria.text: Do AI initiated submissions create the correct request records and enter a working fulfilment process?
criteria.why: Successful conversational intake is insufficient without controlled downstream execution.
criteria.evidence: Test order record, fulfilment owner, approval status and tracking history.
criteria.improve: Fix fulfilment integration and verify record creation and tracking.
criteria.learn: Whether an AI initiated request produces the correct records and can be tracked through real fulfilment.

criteria.text: When a request is unclear or unsupported, does the experience provide safe clarification, form fallback or human escalation?
criteria.why: The system must handle exceptions without inventing or forcing unsafe requests.
criteria.evidence: Ambiguous, cancelled and unsupported request tests and fallback results.
criteria.improve: Document and test the clarification and fallback routes.
criteria.learn: Whether ambiguous or unsupported requests have a safe way to clarify, redirect or reach a human rather than producing an unsuitable request.

responseRubric.yes: The criterion is satisfied in the selected scope. Supporting evidence should be available.
responseRubric.partial: The condition is present in some scenarios, but gaps remain.
responseRubric.no: The criterion is not satisfied in the selected scope.
responseRubric.unknown: Not enough information has been gathered to make a claim.
responseRubric.na: Excluded by the assessor with a written scope justification. This does not confirm the requirement is irrelevant.

evidenceRubric.reviewed: Assessor reports inspecting supporting records or documents.
evidenceRubric.tested: Assessor reports running representative checks. The application does not independently verify these claims.
